source.title: A Regularization-Sharpness Tradeoff for Linear Interpolators

record.file_problem: not stated; full paper text supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a proposed interpolating-information criterion tracks generalization in overparameterized linear regression, using correlations with test MSE and comparisons across feature dimensions and regularizers; this is a different measure and setting from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-MSE comparisons and correlations for interpolating linear regressors. Its neural-network, random-label, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, and memorized-example statements are background citations, not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study tests an information criterion for explicitly norm-selected linear interpolators, not any supplied claim version. V2 concerns widening trained ReLU networks; varying fixed random Fourier or polynomial features in linear regression does not test it. V7 concerns magnitude-scaled weight perturbations and generalization gaps in convolutional networks; the study's geometric IIC component and test-MSE correlations measure different constructs.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they derive IIC decompositions for linear interpolators, propose a regularization–sharpness tradeoff, and identify a sparse case in which both terms can decrease with dimension. They describe IIC as tracking test MSE in most settings and explicitly call the evidence preliminary. That description should remain attributed to the authors: the displayed negative correlations do not establish the same ordering of IIC and test MSE.
record.recipe_differences: Studies overparameterized linear regression with ℓp-regularized interpolators and evaluates IIC/test-MSE relations; claim versions concern neural-network training, interventions, or magnitude-aware generalization measures. Uses random Fourier and polynomial features on real-world datasets.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and feature construction alter the observed IIC/test-MSE relationship and component trends; the text reports an opposite or weaker correlation pattern for several datasets compared with FLIR and a qualitatively different trend for polynomial features.

fits_no_version.finding: IIC has strong positive correlations with test MSE on several datasets and strong negative correlations on others; CIFAR-10 correlations are weaker. Some remaining dataset assignments are uncertain.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In norm-selected linear interpolation with random Fourier features, IIC can have a strong monotonic association with test MSE, but its direction depends on the dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors describe decreasing regularization and increasing geometric sharpness with dimension for smooth penalties, while sparse penalties can make both decrease. Some Table 2 entries conflict with this narrative.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The dimension dependence of the IIC decomposition differs between smooth and sparse norm-selected linear interpolators.

fits_no_version.finding: Polynomial-feature interpolators perform poorly, and the authors report that IIC tracks their test-MSE trend without continuing its RFF decrease.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relationship between IIC, dimension, and prediction quality depends on feature construction in linear interpolation.

record.problems: The authors describe the work as initial support and not conclusive. It uses linear models rather than neural networks. For p>2 the criterion has a dimension upper bound. Table 2's supplied flattened text makes some dataset-to-value assignments unrecoverable. Some reported results are qualitative figure descriptions without numeric values.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results were reported by this study; background citations to neural-network generalization claims were excluded. Table 2 includes entries beyond the FLIR, CIFAR-10, MNIST, FMNIST, CIFAR-100, and SVHN rows that cannot be assigned reliably to the remaining dataset labels from the flattened text; the ambiguous correlations for component-versus-dimension were not extracted as separate rows. Figure 2's qualitative trends for p=2 and p=3 were covered by the authors' conclusion and R13's p=1 diagnostic, but no additional figure-only rows were added.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy under the same neural-network architecture and training recipe.
Test-error changes when trained one-hidden-layer ReLU networks widen beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimization under specified tuning budgets and recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out classifier error across training-set sizes and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus neural-network generalization gaps, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: No version verdicts are warranted. Strong correlation with a different criterion does not test V7, and feature-dimension scaling in explicitly norm-selected linear regression does not test V2. Table ambiguities remain unresolved using the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization in neural networks.
Widening one-hidden-layer ReLU networks beyond interpolation and measuring whether test error continues to fall.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons against norm- and margin-based generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
